testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A visual low pressure warning signal should activate before air pressure drops to between ____ psi.
questions.explanation: A visual low pressure warning signal activates before air pressure drops to 55-75 psi. This signal can be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: When leaving a vehicle unattended, a driver should:

options.text: Only set the parking brake if parked on a slope.

questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when leaving your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: An alcohol evaporator in an air brake system:

options.text: Makes the brakes work without squeaking.
Prevents ice from forming in the braking system.
Lubricates parts of the braking system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevents ice from forming in the braking system.
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator introduces alcohol into the air brake system. The alcohol helps prevent ice from forming inside the system.

questions.question: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have ____ malfunction lamps to show when ABS is not working.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with ABS have yellow malfunction lamps to alert drivers when the braking system is not working. Know where your vehicle's malfunction lamp is located before you drive.

questions.question: The ____ turn on when the brake pedal is pressed.
questions.explanation: In vehicles with air brakes, pressing the brake pedal triggers an electric switch that turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: When you need to make an emergency stop, you should:

options.text: Veer your trailer to the right and stop.
Veer your trailer to the left and stop.

questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, brake in a way that keeps your vehicle in a straight line. This allows you to turn if needed. You can use controlled braking or stab braking methods.

questions.question: Air storage tanks:

options.text: Are not allowed on a vehicle.
Hold compressed air for the brakes.
Should be drained of excess air after every trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold compressed air for the brakes.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air used by the brakes. The number and size of tanks varies by vehicle.

questions.question: When parking, you should not use the parking brake if:

options.text: There is snow on the ground.

questions.explanation: Do not use the parking brake when brakes are hot from coming down a steep grade. Let them cool first to avoid damaging the brakes.

questions.question: Once air tanks reach 125 psi, the air compressor governor will:

options.text: Stop the compressor from pumping air.
Begin pumping air into the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the compressor from pumping air.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor stops pumping air once tanks reach about 125 psi. This level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: Having ABS on only one axle:

options.text: Still gives you more control when braking.
Slows the vehicle but cannot stop it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Still gives you more control when braking.
questions.explanation: Even with ABS on only one axle, you have more braking control than without ABS. Brake normally.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in the air brake system releases air, what does this mean?

options.text: The air pressure is too high.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air pressure is too high.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air when pressure gets too high. If this happens, something is wrong and a mechanic should check the system.

questions.question: What do ABS brakes do?

options.text: Stop your wheels from locking up.
Prevent your vehicle from going uphill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop your wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: When spring brakes are on, you should never:
questions.explanation: Do not push the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. Using both at the same time can damage the brakes.

questions.question: When going downhill, you should brake until you reach a speed that is:
questions.explanation: Going downhill, brake until you reach 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release the brake and repeat this process.

questions.question: In a newer vehicle with air brakes, the parking brake is applied by:

options.text: Moving a lever to the right.

questions.explanation: In newer vehicles, pull the yellow diamond-shaped knob to apply the parking brake. Push it in to release the parking brake.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, you should:
questions.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. Using both together can damage the brakes.

questions.question: Do not drive a vehicle if any brake drum has cracks larger than ____ of the friction area width.
questions.explanation: Check brake drums before every trip. Do not drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than one half of the friction area width.

questions.question: The front brake limiting valve usually has two markings that read:
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles with air brakes have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, what is the safe maximum air loss for a double combination vehicle?
questions.explanation: For a double combination vehicle, air should not leak more than 3 psi in one minute. If it leaks faster, something needs to be repaired before driving.

questions.question: In cold weather, you should check your vehicle's alcohol evaporator:
questions.explanation: The alcohol evaporator prevents ice buildup in the air brake system. Check and refill it every day in cold weather.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in the air brake system releases air, what does this mean?

options.text: Something is wrong with the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Something is wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air when pressure gets too high. If this happens, there is a problem in the system. Have a mechanic check it before driving.

questions.question: When an S-cam turns inside a brake drum, what does it do?

options.text: Pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
Pushes the brake shoes against the brake linings.
Pushes the brake linings against the wheel axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, the S-cam turns and pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This friction slows down your vehicle.

questions.question: What happens if brakes create too much heat?

options.text: The brakes may squeak more than usual.

questions.explanation: Brakes can fade if they get too hot and lose their stopping power. Do not rely only on brakes to slow down. Also use engine braking to help slow your vehicle.

questions.question: You are traveling at 55 mph on dry pavement. How much distance does brake lag add to your stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: What should you do if the low pressure warning signal activates while driving?

options.text: Stop and park where you are
Leave the roadway and park as soon as it is safe

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the roadway and park as soon as it is safe
questions.explanation: If the low pressure warning activates, safely exit the roadway and park your vehicle right away. Low air pressure means your brakes will not work well enough to stop safely.
